title: Bin El Ouidane reservoir, 22 Jun to 8 Oct 2026
summary: Between 22 Jun and 8 Oct 2026 the lake went from 31.35 km2 to 29.91 km2, while the whole circle got brighter, with mean HH up 1.75 dB. The 8 Oct date carries two flags, so this brightening should not be read as change on the ground.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.text: Over 108 days the lake changed by -1.44 km2, or -4.6%. HH turned brighter by more than 3 dB on 41.12 km2 and darker on only 0.1 km2. HV turned brighter on 7.7 km2.

sections.heading: Where, by terrain type
sections.text: The brightening covers every type. Rough dry ground and fields had 18.02 km2 brighter in HH, and trees, shrub and rugged slopes 10.3 km2. Built-up land, which should stay stable, rose 2.33 dB in HH.

sections.heading: Possible causes
sections.text: Possible cause: a processing offset in the 8 Oct product, since buildings brightened like fields; reprocessed files would settle it. Possible cause: a wet surface after rain; local rain records for early October would check it. Possible cause for the lake: summer drawdown; the dam's level records would confirm it.

sections.heading: Limits
sections.text: 8 Oct 2026 carries two flags: the lake water threshold moved more than 1.0 dB from the previous date, and backscatter over built-up land shifted more than 0.5 dB from its June-September median. Both lower confidence in every number from that date. NASA has no NISAR data from 27 Jul to 10 Aug 2026, so nothing between 16 Jul and 21 Aug 2026 is seen.

sections.heading: What an agency could do next
sections.text: Use an unflagged date for a firm end-of-summer lake figure, check rain records for early October, and ask NASA whether the October products will be reprocessed.
